svg.text: Equation 1 has three parts, and the one that does no work is the one that matters

g.data-tip: The output vector of the layers considered. It has the same shape as x, which is what lets these blocks be stacked without any glue between them.
The function the stacked layers actually have to learn. The paper defines it as F(x) := H(x) - x, where H is the mapping you originally wanted.
The block input itself, added back element-wise. It is not transformed, not gated and not scaled, which is why it costs nothing.
Because y must have the same shape as x, a stack of these blocks keeps one width and one map size all the way through a stage: a run of blocks at one feature-map size, conv2_x to conv5_x in Table 1.
g.text: The sum, before the outer ReLU: ReLU(y) exits.
Same shape as x, so blocks stack directly.
One block, not the whole network.

g.data-tip: F can be two or three layers. With one layer only, the paper notes the block is similar to a plain linear layer and it observed no advantage.
g.text: Two layers here: F = W2 . ReLU(W1 x), with
the biases omitted to simplify notation.
The Wi are the block's learnable weights.

g.data-tiphead: Why the identity path is free
g.data-tip: There is no matrix on this path. Nothing is learned, nothing is multiplied, so the shortcut adds neither extra parameter nor computation complexity.
g.text: The input itself, unchanged. No matrix,
no gate, never closed. Hence zero extra

a.data-tip: Performed on two feature maps channel by channel. Every entry of F(x) is added to the entry of x at the same position and channel, so the two tensors must have identical shape.
a.text: Walking one block, shape by shape
block input x
after the first 3x3, 64
after the second 3x3, 64 — this is F(x)
the shortcut hands back x, untouched
F(x) + x, one add per entry
Weights on the shortcut: none. Multiplies on the shortcut: none.
Shapes follow Table 1, conv2_x of the 34-layer net.
224x224 input, halved by the stride-2 conv1 and by max pooling.

a.data-tip: At a stage boundary the channel count doubles and the feature map halves, so x and F(x) no longer have the same shape and cannot be added. Equation 2 inserts a linear projection Ws on the shortcut, done by 1x1 convolutions with a stride of 2.
a.text: When the shapes do not match
y = F(x, {Wi}) + Ws x
Eqn (2)
Eqn (1) needs x and F(x) the same shape. At each stage
boundary both change: channels double and the map halves,
56x56x64 → 28x28x128. Ws is then a 1x1 conv with stride 2.
The paper: Ws is only used when matching dimensions.
